name: AD - Enumerate Security Controls (Defender / AppLocker / CLM)
description: Post-foothold enumeration of host security controls: checks Windows Defender real-time protection state, AppLocker policy rules, and PowerShell Constrained Language Mode. Run these to understand what defenses you are operating against before loading tools.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

variations.label: AppLocker Policy
variations.description: List all effective AppLocker rules — shows which executables and scripts are blocked. Look for PowerShell blocked at system32 path but not SysWOW64 (common bypass)

variations.label: PowerShell CLM Check
variations.description: Returns FullLanguage or ConstrainedLanguage. CLM blocks COM objects, restricts .NET types, and breaks many offensive PowerShell tools — plan around it

variations.label: Firewall + Defender (CMD)
variations.command:
netsh advfirewall show allprofiles
sc query windefend
variations.description: Check firewall state across all profiles and query Windows Defender service status from cmd.exe

examples.label: Confirm if CLM is active (ConstrainedLanguage = restricted)

notes:
=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Defender: RealTimeProtectionEnabled=True → built-in tools or signed LOLBins only
AppLocker: Look for paths NOT blocked — SysWOW64, TEMP, user-writable dirs often missed
CLM: ConstrainedLanguage → many PowerView/PowerUp functions break; use C# or bypass

=== COMMON APPLOCKER BYPASS ===
If system32\powershell.exe is blocked:
  C:\Windows\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe  (32-bit, often missed)
  PowerShell_ISE.exe  (sometimes not in rules)

=== CLM BYPASS APPROACHES ===
  1. PS downgrade: powershell.exe -version 2 (no CLM, no Script Block Logging)
  2. Use compiled C# (runspace bypass)
  3. Use tools that don't rely on PS (SharpHound.exe, etc.)

defense.why_it_works: Native PowerShell cmdlets (Get-MpComputerStatus, Get-AppLockerPolicy) and WMI/SC calls query security product state through legitimate management interfaces. No special privilege needed — any authenticated user can read Defender and AppLocker configuration. This enumeration is completely silent under default logging.
defense.prerequisites: Any authenticated foothold on a domain-joined Windows host.
defense.impact: Intelligence only — tells the attacker what tools will work and what bypasses are needed. Defenders lose advantage when attackers know which controls are active.
defense.detection: Get-MpComputerStatus and Get-AppLockerPolicy generate no dedicated security events under default config. PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event 4104) records the commands if enabled and if the attacker has not downgraded to PS v2. Sysmon Event 1 with powershell.exe parent + these cmdlet names can serve as IOCs.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell Operational log (4104) if Script Block Logging is enabled. No network artifacts — all local queries.
defense.prevention: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging and Transcription (GPO: Computer Config → Admin Templates → Windows Components → PowerShell). Deploy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint which detects enumeration patterns. Enforce PowerShell v5+ only (disable v2 via: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root).
defense.evasion: Downgrade to PS v2 (`powershell.exe -version 2`) to evade Script Block Logging. Use cmd.exe equivalents (`sc query windefend`, `netsh advfirewall`) to avoid PowerShell logging entirely.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Default Windows: No Script Block Logging
# PowerShell v2 still installed (older systems):
Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2
# State: Enabled  -> v2 available for downgrade

# No alerting on Get-MpComputerStatus by default:
# Defender itself doesn't flag enumeration of its own status
defense.secure_config:
# Disable PowerShell v2:
Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root

# Enable Script Block Logging (GPO or registry):
$key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging'
New-Item $key -Force
Set-ItemProperty $key -Name EnableScriptBlockLogging -Value 1

# Enforce AppLocker in Enforcement mode (not Audit mode):
Set-AppLockerPolicy -XMLPolicy <policy.xml> -Merge
defense.misconfiguration: AppLocker deployed in Audit mode (logs but does not block). Only blocking system32\powershell.exe while SysWOW64 and PowerShell_ISE.exe paths are not included. Script Block Logging enabled but PowerShell v2 not removed — v2 bypasses logging.

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

recommended.note: If tools are blocked, switch to LOTL techniques using built-in Windows commands
